So, which came first, S/D or PA? Or of course, S/R To me, there's no difference between them. Both are simply decisions made on the value of an asset and what happens to price when it returns to these decision points. Price simply bounces from decision point to decision point. The following user(s) said Thank You: Steigo, omidfxt, salivan, staurum QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA #256 MitchWorse Offline Trader Posts: 172 Thank you received: 202 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=250 6/32 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 11 - RTM Community <nerdmHodOeM> E EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT supply && demand == market The name of this topic describes the understanding of price in its purest form. When 2 people want to buy 1 available object, the object will go to the highest bid. Demand > Supply, price goes up. When 2 people want to sell an identical object and there is 1 buyer who needs 1 object, the buyer will go for the lowest ask. Supply > Demand, price goes down. When there is no supply or demand, there is no price. When you look at a chart with price history(from any object), you will spot recent levels at which price reacted; A base/range where buyers and sellers agreed on price followed by an impulse. That impulse was triggered by a decision that caused supply and demand to go out of balance. The level where this decision was made should be marked on your chart. There will be supply or demand left at that zone. When buyers and sellers disagree on price, price will move to a previous level of agreement. How price moves between levels is called Price Action(PA). Since price is based on the opinions from buyers and sellers and not solely on facts, trading can't be science, therefor it must be an art. </nerdmode> :whistle: https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=250 7/32 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 14 - RTM Community THANK YOU EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT HOME SD/SR/Flip Zones help needed #328 Simon Offline Trader Posts: 252 Thank you received: 180 I feel like there are many trading opportunities that I am missing, particularly the intraday ones. I've noticed that there seems to be quite a lot of emphasis on S/R "flip zones", and traders advocating touch-trades at the first test. One thing that I have found confusing with this is that in order to establish a horizontal line at the flip-zone one will need to cut through candles. Sam Seiden, who I would consider my trading mentor has offered many examples of the areas that he considers supply or demand. And crucially, one will often hear Sam say that in order to mark out the level, "We NEVER cut through candles". The one person who made total sense to me from day one of my trading journey is Sam Seiden. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT If a demand gets broken, and price shoots down from it, we look for the point where the decision was made to break it. Ideally we look for a break, and then a rally back into it which fails miserably. This "Epic Fail" point is the decision that price has broken the level and the level is staying broken. We can't just expect price to break this DP easily, as lots of sell orders await price's return there. That's why price will often need to bounce from S/R flips back to the last DP before advancing. In the case of your chart, the Deman you have shown is a reaction to something on the left - the decision to break a beautiful Supply. See what happened lately when price came back up from your buy line and hit that old supply? Thanks, QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA #364 Tyoon Offline Elite Trader Posts: 331 Thank you received: 407 rokuhaato wrote: If price form a flag before reaching S or D area, what does it 15/31 mean and how to deal with it? https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=350 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 15 - RTM Community I am sorry if I am in the wrong thread to ask. MORE HOME EDUCATION FORUM LOGOUT When you see something that looks like a flag before a level, it is most likely consumption of that level. So if you see a buflag at supply it could be that the buyers are consuming the supply orders to break through. If you think of a level of supply and a level of demand (or support and resistance), price either consumes one level and rejects off of the other. So price can be consuming supply then rejecting off of demand. So, the way to deal with it is to find your levels and watch the PA interaction between them within the flag keeping the bigger picture in mind. If I could speak in this debate, I would say that zone engulf and candle engulf have practically the same meaning. The only thing to which you should pay attention to is the time (or time frame). Example of this is HTF engulf which on LTF looks like zone engulf. This is most evident on H4 TF where we can see different candle close depending on the time zone of the broker. In this scenario we could see engulf formed from one candle in one broker feed and from two candles in other brokers feed. But when we see it in LTF they are just the same zone engulf. IMO if you remember about this important detail we can use both approaches equally. :) What are your arguments in this debate? Posts: 257 Thank you received: 427 WRB: Wide Range Bodies = BIG CANDLES, lots of orders, heavy money making the price move fast and wild. Hidden gaps: there is no space between the candles, so it is not a true gap. HOWEVER, a WRB candle is called a hidden gap because this very candle must be filled, some people are trapped at the other end of it because it moved too fast. I personnally call them price inconsistencies. The price action is not clean, price has not been retest. In the way we teach here, hidden gaps are the sources of the poles (you know, poles, flag?). A flag fills the pole and comes back to source. Then the hiddne gap is closed and price can resume in the same direction. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=425 28/31 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 18 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT extremerrage wrote: E good day , out of topic what is WRB and hidden gaps ?? Just trying to get my head around it all. Regards Marc Hi Marc, What you are asking is really about the basics of supply and demand trading and it's important that you understand it. I wrote an article about Basic Supply & Demand some time ago , you can find it here: www.acegazette.com/en/trading-articles/s...s-levels-by-mel.html This is important to know that price moves from Supply to Demand and from Demand to Supply. Why does price move from Demand to Supply? Simply because Buyers were in control at this particular point. Why does price move from Supply to Demand? Simply because Sellers were in control at this particular point. Why is it that price can break Supply and become Demand? Simply because Buyers were in control at this particular point. Why is it that price can break Demand and become Supply? Simply because Sellers were in control at thos particular point. Our edge is based on this simple facts. When price re-visit a Fresh Demand, we look to buy because there is a good chance that Big Money will have orders placed there and vice versa for a re-vist of a Fresh Supply. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=550 16/36 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 23 - RTM Community I suspect that the "brief pause" you are reffering to is what we call a Base. You can find HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT more info about it by clicking on the link to the article. Now about the Swing high and low, imo, those are mostly just retests of a previous Supply & Demand areas... I have marked a chfjpy chart for you with some thoughts on it, Hopefully it helps. When I first started to look at Supply and HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Demand, I did so many "researches" on my charts in order to locate some "bases" /S/D . Then, I remember hearing Sam S. talking about Fresh zones in his video and this is when the "troubles" started for me. I looked at the zones I had marked on my charts and they all seemed to be not fresh....! I can tell you, I was scratching my head because I wanted to know why all the bases were already tested lol After looking and searching, I realized that there was something very intresting and powerfull that happened all the time on the charts. A supply took place, was tested once, retested twice (sometimes more) and bammmme the magic happened...... This Supply BECAME Demand! (and vice versa for Demand becoming Supply) You see, for something to be called Fresh, it has to be New, untouched and how in the world is this going to happen ? Well I concluded that a Fresh zone can only exists when there is a swap in decision. IF did a video about Decision Point, it helped me understand it even more. When a new decision is made, you'll see a Decision point/ base forming and this is when a Fresh Supply/Demand exists. Posts: 463 Thank you received: 910 I'll have a go. To be a true FTR of the S/R line you have marked, it should not manage to get back above the that same S/R line. However, as the decision to break and go low is an engulf, you should always be aware that it can retrace up to the supply which created the engulf - the "source". When price moves away from this area for some time, and then returns, the FTR below the S/R line is a preferable touch trade, as if the FTR is created higher (red) then you have to then consider that price is moving up to stacked zones, so you need to watch PA more carefully. Also, if you use the red FTR as your entry point on the FTB then you shall also need to consider that you have broken the S/R line to the upside, and so that line has now become a demand zone, which reduces your R:R for your first TG. Maybe this makes it clearer: https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=1200 25/31 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 49 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT The following user(s) said Thank You: snebucA, harshrthakkar, Jambowlyai, briantv, omidfxt, salivan, staurum, cuimingzhao Roads? QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA #1279 jogold24 Offline Trader Posts: 57 Thank you received: 34 Traders helping traders :) a'lot of people ask questions on this site, and no one really gives straight out answers, so i will try and clarify my insight and knowledge that i gained from a great trader and friend and all praise goes out to him (redsword) https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=1275 7/39 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 52 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT what iv'e learnt and seen for my self, are that markets are very simple by nature. so don't try and complicate things which i tend to sometimes do. in general, price move's from source to source, that is, Supply & Demand. ASK YOUR SELF, what is supply and what does price do at supply. ask your self the same thing at Demand. chart im showing below is silver 4h bare chart, no lines no markings, nothing. before continuing check out the chart, and try and spot the "Demand (first source) & Supply (second source)" (silver 4H) chartupload.com/images/19502173077647496207.png after looking at it, have you spotted the supply & demand? now continuing from above, price moves from source to source. what i mean by that is price will want to move back to the source. the source is where trades are made, placed, entered, what ever you want to call it. that is where you look at to enter/renter the market. chart below are the supply & demand marked out. chartupload.com/images/31578998783755156644.png looking at the source and the candles them self's, we need to find buyers and sellers. as the famous saying goes, "price does not move with out "engulfing". do u see at the source, engulfing candles marked out in red and blue? do u see how price moves away hard from there in White marked out? now this is the first part, spotting credible and reliable levels. the second part is going down a TF or a few TF, and looking at the micro structure of PA with in the marked out levels. this is the tricky part thou since levels (or source) can be at higher or lower levels that u marked out. so u need to spend time at the charts reading, reading and more reading, the charts that is and its structure. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=1275 8/39 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 52 - RTM Community it u look closely at the zoomed in chart, u will see "flips" at the Demand and supply. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT what i mean by flips, is at the demand u will get an r/s flip (resistance turned support) and at supply u will get a s/r flip (support turned resistance). that is the source. that is where you look to enter the trade. chartupload.com/images/47457093265920484275.png this is the simple nature and most common form of PA that moves from "source to source" understand what i talk about and see it for your self and you are well on your way to being a successful trader two example's or trades at the source chartupload.com/images/04305983793326678130.png chartupload.com/images/94126533463886997901.png that's it........... a failed trade u would know with in a very short period of time. at supply, price needs massive liquidity to break up and u would sometimes see it as a engulfing candle to the up side. example below. same goes for Demand with LQG break. if u fail a trade then u read price incorrectly and failed to see the hole picture in all TF. chartupload.com/images/23669224368775212263.png hope i helped a little :) happy trading. What I can say is that when I am not sure, I step back and try and absorb what the bigger picture is telling me and place any potential LTF trade opportunity within the context of the HTF. I am also aware that we should not trade mid-range and we should trade only the edge of the zone. I know that price is typically guided by Flag Limits (FL) and it's the break of the FL that's important as it allows prices to move into a new zone; and the FL defines the edge of the zone. As such I am starting to see FL as my guiding compass, telling me where price wants to go. If done properly, from my limited studies, you can look at the FL in each time frame to keep in the right side of the market at all times to ensure you are trading in the right direction and from the edge of the zone. At present, the Time Frame (TF) that makes sense to me is the H4. I can see how the FL marked is containing price. When a FL breaks, price will often flag and the FL defines the edge of the flag. I want to see price as flags and poles as that is how IF sees price and I want to see price the same way IF does. As such, by what I have marked on the H4 chart below, I can see that I am mid-range on this time frame and nowhere near the edge of a zone that makes sense to me. For this reason, I'd be hesitant to risk my luck (gamble) on any LTF trade unless it made complete sense to me within the LTF; the risk was well defined; and the risk to reward ratio was prime. On your charts start by focusing on the B's (the bases) in those formations and extend them out as far as they seem to matter. Regarding your yellow circles, why did you draw them there? Don't tell us, show us by using boxes on your own chart and extending them to the right to see what happens. Don't be afraid to drop to lower time frames (LTF) and refine your areas of supply and demand. As for how wide to draw them, stop and think about what is really happening as you're doing this homework - real buying and selling is creating the picture on the chart. So in the pic I uploaded, the blue supply box is drawn around the area where buying and selling was fairly equal right before a clear decision by the market to take price lower. That's essentially what a base is: balance in price before clear imbalance, in this case price moved sideways and then selling far exceeded buying, which always means that price must fall. It also might help to think of it as decisions (If has a whole video on it that is phenomenal!) - where did the market make clear decisions on price? That's a base and for this homework it's what you want to mark. An MPL is inside an FTR/FL, it is the extreme set of unfilled orders. An FTR is made (and confirmed) once a new high (HH) or low (LL) is made after a break of some barrier (SR etc...). So without HH in case of the above chart there is no FTR and thus no MPL. Also this, not all QMs are MPLs but an MPL (inside an FTR/FL) can be a QM. As staurum said, this is really explained everywhere on this site and especially in the videos/webinars. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT You've highlighted the typical dangers of patterns - traders tend to see patterns too frequently and see what they want to see rather than what is actually there. This is one of the reasons understanding what is actually happening in patterns like flags in terms of the price action helps to assess the 'quality' of the pattern and the likelihood of it working out. The most common mistake I see people make (not on here - just generally) is with regards H&S patterns, people see them in all shapes and sizes without regard of the location relative to other TF's and to the market generally - let alone an understanding on what is actually occurring in an H&S pattern from a true price action perspective. You've also highlighted the nuances off going from a relatively quiet session (Asia) to Frankfurt / London open - it's easy to see Asian low liquidity and thus tight consolidation as a flag or other pattern, taking care when you are approaching such a big jump in volume is always prudent IMO. With regards flags specifically, another thing I would generally comment on is to 16/36 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=175 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 8 - RTM Community remember what a flag is: HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 1. It's a continuation of a strong momentum move - it's a brief pause while price clears demand (for a short setup) and then moves on it's way. Thus it is logical that if the pole forms say over 2 hours and then price consolidates in the flag for 12 hours then the 'chances' of the flag working have somewhat decreased - because you're looking for that same momentum (which is a strong supply / demand imbalance) being present and price moving in the same vein it did when forming the pole. 2. The chances of a flag also working out if it retraces the whole pole distance are also decreased, why, because as a I said above a flag is a momentum continuation move so if price is retracing the whole move what does that tell us about the strength of the move that caused the pole - that supply / demand imbalance has been completely retraced. Of course that latter could turn out to be compression back into the source of the pole for example, but then that's something different and not a flag. I find when first understanding patterns if people (a) remember to think about what the pattern represents should be happening (b) understand the price action occurring within the pattern (c) remember to check the location and surrounding TF's and (d) check the market generally it helps to keep them out of trouble and focussing on identifying the more straight forward and obvious setups which helps to build confidence before moving onto more advanced concepts. Quickly scanned the charts to find two examples of more obvious straightforward flags. Notice how price moved after it forms the flag lows/highs i.e. hits supply for the short and demand for the long (you should always be able to identify a clear supply / demand zone where price will start to move with high momentum and breakout of the flag). The advantage of having the above knowledge is you know how price should move and where it should move from and thus can get into a trade at the biggest discount and easily cut the trade when price isn't doing what it should. Catching moves like this when you're in at the source of the flag provide some very big risk/reward opportunities. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=175 17/36 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 8 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=175 18/36 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 8 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Attachments: https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=175 19/36 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 8 - RTM Community The following user(s) said Thank You: FX.Sniffer, Les_Paul, okami, Steigo, windorz, masut, HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT staurum QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA #189 Tyoon Offline Elite Trader Posts: 331 Thank you received: 407 Josh wrote: let alone an understanding on what is actually occurring in an H&S pattern from a true price action perspective. Josh wrote: You've also highlighted the nuances off going from a relatively quiet session (Asia) to Frankfurt / London open - it's easy to see Asian low liquidity and thus tight consolidation as a flag or other pattern, taking care when you are approaching such a big jump in volume is always prudent IMO. Asian session are not typically low in liquidity. They only seem like that because they usually run their circular trade phase to build positions for the European opens. When the rolls are switched the Asians can make very large moves just like you would see in typical NY and London sessions. If Asians do stick to a tight range the key is to watch how the range widens during Franky and London open. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/classroom-and-trading-room/33-supply-and-demand-support-and-resistance-pa?start=175 20/36 7/27/2018 Supply and Demand, Support and Resistance, PA - Page 8 - RTM Community JoshHwOroMteE: With reEgDarUdCs AflaTgIsOsNpecificalFlyO, aRnUoMther thingMIOwRouEld geneLraOllyGOUT comment on is to remember what a flag is A flag is either one of two things; profit taking or consumption. Why do you see constantly flags at key levels before they break? At key levels there are a crap load of orders sitting there (lovely liquidity) in which the market makers take advantage of to re- accumulate. If they were net long for example and price gets to a level of sell orders, they use it as an opportunity to add to their positions - consuming them. When they get to their level of taking profits they will release their longs as sales into the market which creates a beflag pattern. It consolidates but does not drop too much because they release them slowly to keep it within a price range to maintain profit.
